## Body

ROUND 1 performance verdict: PASS-WITH-NOTES.
Subject: pr:331
Head: 0a8490fc85894b394f4d268b3971e72f605c7a9a
Answers: 01a1ff91-05d4-79a0-bb9a-1c2f661274e5

The real drain now avoids walking/decoding the retired seat history. Source, exact-query EXPLAIN and CI support that improvement. No new loop, timer, process launch or per-seat worker is added. No demonstrated normal-use resource-cost breach blocks this head. Two qualifications are required: the owed arm visits ALL open jobs, and the7.53/.86ms measurement is a Python roster/peek benchmark, not a Rust drain tick.

Verified source/plan cost:
- Existing registry call is replaced, not supplemented: one schema check and one roster SELECT, followed by the same kind filtering/peek/dispatch paths. The default5s drain cadence and existing lease-deadline wake path are unchanged.
- seats_live is a partial(id) index for tombstoned_at IS NULL. Its scan visits live rows L; the historical retired seat table is not scanned.
- jobs_claimable covers(state, kind, id). EXPLAIN narrows it by state only: SEARCH jobs USING COVERING INDEX jobs_claimable(state=?). The substr(kind...) predicates are residual. Every pending/running index row Q is tested, including non-delivery queues; closed job history is skipped. Thus "O(live + open delivery rows)" is too narrow.
- Delivery/control target IDs are derived from kind, distincted through a temp B-tree, then looked up in seats by primary key under CROSS JOIN. The owed arm also uses a temp B-tree for ORDER BY. Budget L+ALL open-job candidate work, distinct/order work and D distinct-target primary-key lookups; full descriptor decode is only for returned live/retired-owed rows. Row-count reduction alone is not the whole cost model.
- Exact-source query, schema50, SQLite3.54.1, private in-memory fixture:20 live+3 owed returned23 rows in969 VM instructions. Adding2,000 unrelated OPEN jobs kept23 rows but raised work to20,962 instructions. Adding2,000 unrelated DONE jobs or2,000 retired seats owed nothing did not increase that instruction count. This is candidate-work evidence, not elapsed-time/Rust performance.
- Independently dropping seats_live or jobs_claimable in that private fixture made the query fail explicitly with "no such index". No silent full-scan fallback exists. The real adapter propagates query errors to the drain's existing error path.
- Fakes use the unchanged whole-roster default, a superset; they do not prove optimized real-store timing. Shared kind-prefix constants preserve the strings. Park notice and the PA watchdog are unchanged here, deliberately retaining their current work/scope.
- #328's late-error change adds a log line on an already-failing lease read and still returns None. No extra lease read/retry is added. The new doc correctly names the one-shot shared boot deadline and up to two guards' SQL/native-lock work, without a restart-latency ceiling.

Copy benchmark scope:
- Falcon supplied the retrospectively saved eval-cell code/docstring in f259a-drain-bench.py. Reported copy:3,297 seats,133 live;241 pending+136 running jobs. Old/new medians over50 iterations:7.53/.86ms; returned rows3297/302 and kind strings1992/275.
- I read the code, did not rerun it. Each timed iteration is Python sqlite3 roster execute/fetchall(row materialization), a Python implementation of the kinds filter, json.dumps(kinds), then peek SQL/fetchone. It does NOT run Rust row_to_descriptor, schema/pool/async overhead, tmux, claim or handle_claim.
- No drain kind had an open job on that snapshot: both intersections were equal and EMPTY. This establishes the sampled empty-peek preparation case, not matching productive dispatch behavior under load. The original copy is gone and there is no separate original execution log; the figures are author-reported, with the saved code/output inspected.
- At nominal720 scheduled ticks/hour, those medians project to about5.42s/.62s of cumulative elapsed PYTHON preparation time, not measured SQL-only time or daemon CPU. No full Rust/live8.8x improvement or future10k-row ceiling is asserted.
